page: Amazon Web Services g5g.8xlarge is an ARM64-based server instance powered by 32 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. This instance features a bundled NVIDIA T4G GPU from the Turing family with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM, designed for graphics-intensive and machine learning workloads. No local NVMe SSD storage is included in this configuration.

Benchmark results place the g5g.8xlarge in the average performance tier for most multi-core and memory operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score is 48574.86, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 11551.0, both falling within the middle 50% of tested servers. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with a Geekbench single-core score of 952.0 and a weak single-threaded gzip compression speed of 20.17 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show a high read-only small block cached speed of 1892.97 GB/sec, but a lower large block uncached write speed of 72.88 GB/sec. For language model tasks, the server achieves an average prompt processing speed of 31.98 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model, though text generation on a small 135M model is poor at 42.38 tokens/sec.

The g5g.8xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for GPU-accelerated workloads by leveraging the ARM64 architecture, which typically delivers high resource density and lower power consumption compared to x86 alternatives. The dedicated core allocation and Nitro hypervisor ensure consistent execution. This server is suited for entry-level machine learning inference, ray tracing, software compilation, and static web serving, where multi-threaded ARM efficiency and GPU acceleration can be utilized without requiring local high-speed storage.
